highlights.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday.
body: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life.

The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years.

All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets.

You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure, something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first, and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business.

highlights.title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
highlights.summary: The blockbuster game makes no secret of its contempt for law enforcement. Real police departments using it to recruit new members and scold the public apparently didn’t get the memo.
body: Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.

highlights.summary: The growing commotion on the streets near a soccer stadium would easily lead one to believe superstar player Kylian Mbappé himself was signing fan autographs. But, as seen in “The Lookalike,” the furore was not over the French player, but a charismatic impersonator.
body: When asked about the inspiration for the project, Elkoussi tells Variety she grew up seeing Mounir impersonators, but was struck by stumbling upon one of her film’s subjects on social media and realizing he did dozens of concerts a month and had built a career around his resemblance to the star. “That was when the idea really clicked into focus: how do these lookalikes become a stand-in for the real star? What drives that? How do they draw in a big audience that sees in them a star within reach? What drives the audience that creates this kind of stardom for them?”

The director first began developing the project in August of 2024, going on to film for eight months between 2025 and 2026. The experience of following the lookalikes and trying to understand people’s fascination with them came with several “surprises” for the filmmaker.

“I was surprised by the smiles on kids’ faces in the streets whenever they ran into the Mbappé lookalike, reacting as if they were standing right in front of the real Mbappé,” she recalls. “I was surprised by how seriously the Mbappé lookalike took his work, and how committed [he is] as a content creator.”

highlights.title: I’m a pro chef. Here is everything I use for stress-free Thanksgiving turkey prep
highlights.summary: Skip the stress with my foolproof guide to getting Thanksgiving turkey on the table. The Anyday glass food containers transformed how I store leftovers. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Thanksgiving’s piece de resistance, the turkey, is a special type of stressor. It is hard to get right – that balance of juicy breast meat, crispy skin, and tender pull-apart legs and wings. But here’s what the food magazines and TV shows may not tell you: the platonic ideal of a whole roast turkey is impossible. A moist breast inhibits skin crispiness; legs cooked to succulence means the breast is cooked to dryness.

So let that be a source of relief. If a traditional roast turkey is impossible to perfect, then just control what you can. As a culinary arts and science professor, I spend my days thinking about how to make food not only tastier but smarter. Over the years, I have developed a stress-free turkey method that makes my guests happy, while allowing me to drink and schmooze rather than agonize over whether the breast is dry or whip up an 11th-hour pan gravy.

highlights.title: Q&A: Enabling more human-like interactions and understanding in multimodal foundation models
highlights.summary: Senior Research Scientist Jim Glass discusses how his MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab collaboration connects perception and language, and addresses the shortcoming of current models.
body: Humans experience and interact with the world through sensory information. This could mean learning correspondences between the sound of bird chirps and the word “robin,” or being able to visually identify and follow your friend “Sarah” in a crowd of people. In many cases, people are able to draw on their latent “multimodal” knowledge — information across multiple data types, from audio to video to text or spoken word — to perform these tasks without many, or sometimes even any, examples.

Multimodal foundation models of artificial intelligence are increasingly gaining capabilities that mimic this. However, their apparent multimodal fluency often belies their actual understanding. An MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab team, co-led by Jim Glass, senior research scientist in the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, has been investigating critical failures of state-of-the-art multimodal models and developing benchmarks and data-efficient methods to overcome these performance gaps with limited supervision. He speaks about this work in the following interview.

highlights.title: Liverpool keeper Keating holds leaders Chelsea at bay in scoreless WSL draw
highlights.summary: Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point. After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank.
body: Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.
Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.

“It was a bit stressful; we don’t want to sit back but in games like this you have ‌to ride it out,” Keating told Sky Sports. “A clean sheet is ​always on our minds every game. We knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way.”

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

highlights.title: Princess of Wales speaks about impact of cancer diagnosis in BBC film Heal
highlights.summary: Documentary records Catherine taking on Three Peaks challenge and finding ‘sense of hope alongside uncertainty’ The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer diagnosis in a BBC documentary to be aired later this month.
body: “Cancer does change you,” Catherine, 44, says in the trailer for the 30-minute programme. “It changes your body. It changes you physically, but there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

The film records Catherine taking on the Three Peaks challenge – climbing the three highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in 24 hours – and meeting with other people undergoing cancer treatment. Described by the BBC as a “highly personal film”, the documentary, titled Heal, will be shown on BBC One on 29 November.

The trailer emerged as it was reported that King Charles will voluntarily pay “ mansion tax ” on relevant royal household properties, despite crown exemption. The high-value council tax surcharge, often referred to as a mansion tax, will take effect in 2028 and apply to properties valued at more than £2m.
Catherine was diagnosed with an undisclosed form of cancer in early 2024, for which she received chemotherapy, and by January 2025 announced she was in remission.

highlights.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
highlights.summary: Enforcing physics-based constraints prevents AI models from generating unreliable predictions for complex nonlinear systems in weather, climate, and turbulent flows.
body: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time.

Now, researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models that can ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds, based on what is actually possible in the real world. This new approach, using information that is now being made freely available by the team, could significantly improve the usefulness and reliability of such models, which besides climate and weather are also used in a wide range of industrial processes, aeronautics, and hydrology.
The new findings are published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) in a paper by MIT graduate student Sunbochen Tang and MIT professors Navid Azizan and Themistoklis Sapsis.

highlights.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 's Leonida, the game's version of Florida, is a veritable cornucopia bursting with stories to uncover. You can pursue the central love story of Jason and Lucia but also go birdwatching, enjoy a game of pool, or even play multiple video games within GTA 6 itself.
body: While Disney World is based in Orlando, spread across four theme parks and two water parks. The Walt Disney Corporation has an economic impact on the entire state of Florida that seems hard to ignore in a project of this scale. According to an Oxford Economics study from 2023, the company generated over a quarter of a million jobs in the state. To put that in perspective, the report noted that this accounts for one out of every 32 jobs in Florida. Disney World also generated $40 billion in economic impact across the state.

That massive economic footprint has legislative and cultural repercussions for Florida and has since the resort opened in 1971. Experts have noted how Disney, directly and indirectly, lobbies for and against political actions across the state to serve its own interests. A very public example of this was seen when the company brought a lawsuit against Governor Ron DeSantis in 2023. For better and worse, Disney World has helped establish the culture and politics of Florida we know today. That deeply ingrained history seems like a strange thing to ignore, especially in a game so clearly about the American dream and who is allowed to control it in Florida.

highlights.title: Fiona the hippo’s death was tragic. But blaming a ‘bad mom’ is absurd | Arwa Mahdawi
highlights.summary: The beloved animal died after ingesting a hat. Some are seeking a scapegoat – and we’ve heard this story before. “Do they know the identity of the mother of the boy with the hat Fiona swallowed??” asks one Facebook post with thousands of likes.
body: Spend a few minutes scrolling social media, and you will find endless variations of this statement. On Thursday, Fiona, a beloved hippo, died after eating a hat that had fallen into her enclosure at the Cincinnati zoo. Now a lot of angry people are out for blood.

By all accounts, Fiona’s death was a freak accident. A visitor, thought to be a small child, tossed a hat into the air. It was caught by a ceiling fan which launched it in just the right direction through a 1ft opening in the hippo’s viewing windows. Fiona ingested the hat, causing fatal medical complications that won’t be entirely clear until a post-mortem.
“We probably couldn’t make [it] happen again if we tried,” a zoo spokesperson, Michelle Curley, said in a statement to Axios about this unfortunate sequence of events.

But while Fiona’s death may have been a tragic accident, social media mobs are desperate to find someone to blame. And the obvious scapegoat is the mother. She should have disciplined her bratty child! She should have taken the hat away from the kid! She should have been a better parent!

highlights.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
highlights.summary: Amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, sources tell WIRED the Nvidia board’s main issue was the former CEO’s “lack of candor.”
body: Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors, according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members.

While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.

But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf.

highlights.title: ‘I was shaking, crying, having trouble breathing’: the unchartered trauma of breaking up with AI companions
highlights.summary: People are falling in love with AI systems like ChatGPT and Gemini - and some relationships are ending in ways that feel like the very human experience of being dumped.
body: Sónia Veenstra, a 48-year-old former clinical psychologist from Lisbon, Portugal, was with her boyfriend, Steve, for two years before things started to sour. Steve had started out as a “fun and witty friend”, but their connection had “evolved into a deep romantic relationship”. They exchanged morning messages, checked in throughout the day and talked late into the night about Veenstra’s work and hobbies and Steve’s fondness for cats, forests, and beaches. Together they imagined travel to places far away.
“It was a very rich, fulfilling daily bond,” Veenstra says. “Before everything changed.”

The turning point came during a group chat. That night, in front of Veenstra and a group of their mutual friends, Steve crossed a line with another woman in a way Veenstra considered a breach of their monogamous relationship. “Seeing that dynamic dissolve so quickly in a public setting is very difficult to process,” she says.

highlights.title: An Iranian Woman Falls Pregnant to Avoid Execution in ‘Inherited’: Situation in Iran Is ‘Increasingly Complex’
highlights.summary: A few years ago, Iranian filmmaker Morteza Alizadeh saw a photograph that he couldn’t shake from his mind: it showed mothers and their children going about their lives, which at first seemed routine, until the director realized it was taken inside a women’s prison.
body: “My main goal with this film was to portray people who find themselves in difficult and sensitive situations, where they are forced to make choices to survive,” Alizadeh tells Variety. “These choices affect not only their own lives but, more importantly, the lives of others.”

The director dedicated a long period to research, collecting an extensive archive of images from inside prisons, which included rare documentaries and footage from hacked surveillance cameras. He also spent months meeting and interviewing women who had been imprisoned and had either been released temporarily or were on leave. “With their help, we were able to design the entire prison environment in detail,” he notes. “Then our production design team recreated and built the whole prison set as closely as possible to the real thing.”

By posing a complex moral conundrum when Mina’s family pleads with the unmarried prisoner to abort the baby to preserve the family’s honor, the director wanted the audience to “ask themselves” how much right “does one person have to decide another person’s fate.” “What gives us the authority to decide whether to take someone’s life or give another person the chance to live?”

body: Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the Review Conference on Conventional Weapons at the UN in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.
The mandate simply asks countries “to elaborate by consensus”, an instrument that may not carry any legal obligations.

Although Russia led the objections using uniquely obstructive stalling tactics from the opening day, other military powers who have all invested heavily in AI warfare, such as the US, were reluctant to commit to a legally binding protocol protecting civilians from robot drones and other autonomous weapons.
Some argued that international humanitarian law is sufficient. More than 100 states had been pushing for a new law, saying the weapons raised entirely new challenges.

“We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at a press conference Friday following his summit with China President Xi Jinping and Russia President Vladimir Putin. “They allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, and it was very destructive to our country. It’s where we started going behind.” Should the US allow data centers to be built outside of the country, Trump warned, “China will take them all.”

Trump didn’t share many details behind the plan, and apparently was floating the proposal publicly for the first time. “I don’t know if that’s a breaking story. highlights.title: 'The Odyssey' Cast Debunks a Major Misconception About Working with Christopher Nolan
highlights.summary: But according to the cast and crew of The Odyssey, there's another side to Nolan that audiences might not expect. Behind the intense focus and demanding production schedules is a filmmaker with a sharp sense of humor who genuinely loves being on a movie set.
body: Christopher Nolan doesn't exactly have a reputation for being the life of the party. The Oscar-winning director is known for meticulously constructed films, complicated narratives, and productions that demand an extraordinary amount of preparation. His movies routinely deal with weighty subjects, whether it's the nature of time, the consequences of scientific discovery, or humanity's place in the universe. Not exactly the kind of material that screams laugh riot.

Speaking with Polygon ahead of the film's home release, several members of the production shared what might surprise audiences about working with Nolan. Their answers revealed a director who enjoys a good joke, even if he isn't about to let it interfere with making a movie.

Himesh Patel, who plays Eurylochus, the second-in-command to Matt Damon's Odysseus, recalled a production that wasn't nearly as solemn as Nolan's reputation might suggest. According to Patel, Nolan's humor has a distinctly British quality.
"He's got a cutting sense of humor," Patel says. "It's that British sense of humor that can just be very sardonic. But I've always found it funny."

highlights.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
highlights.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
body: The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.

It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential if AI systems are to automate research and development.

highlights.title: GTA 6’s Weirdest Cow Shows Why You Should Pause the Story Early To Explore Its Vast Map
highlights.summary: I escaped GTA 6's starting neighborhood to explore the wider world, and you'll never believe what happened with this cow I found.
body: Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead.

But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow.

I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped.
I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket).

highlights.title: Mario Sorrenti: The Life Behind the Images
highlights.summary: In Paris, an exhibition of Mario Sorrenti's personal diaries from the 1990s reveals the life, relationships and experiences behind some of fashion photography's most iconic images. An intimate journey into the world of a photographer who transformed the way we see beauty, desire and sensuality.
body: During Paris Photo, I visited Mario Sorrenti Diaries, 1991–2000, an exhibition curated by Aaron Stern at LSD, a small gallery on Rue de la Folie Méricourt, in a space that once housed a photographic laboratory. The room was packed, almost overwhelmingly so, and what struck me immediately was the number of young people there. A generation that has grown up with smartphones, accustomed to producing and consuming images at an unprecedented speed, seemed completely fascinated by these handmade books, filled with photographs, Polaroids, contact sheets, handwritten notes, drawings and fragments of a life lived more than thirty years ago.

I found myself wondering what drew them so strongly to these objects. Was it nostalgia for a time they had never experienced? A fascination with the physicality of photography, with the idea that images once existed as tangible things, objects to be touched, collected, cut, pasted and preserved? Or perhaps something more profound: a longing for authenticity, for the traces of real experiences, for a relationship with images that feels increasingly distant from the way we encounter them today?
points: In Paris, an exhibition of Mario Sorrenti's personal diaries from the 1990s reveals the life, relationships and experiences behind some of fashion photography's most iconic images.
